title: Platform control plane ops sketch — midweek notes & open items
content:
Midweek ops sketch for the control plane — intended as a short working doc for the routing/auth/quota sync. Informal notes, sketches, and next steps.

Date: 2026-08-30
Time: 10:30–11:00 PT (midweek deep-dive slot)
Location: #platform-controlplane (call + huddle room)
Attendees: Nina, Marco, Priya, Omar, Lydia (plus async notes from Rahul)

Agenda:
- Quick metrics pulse: latency, quota rejections, auth error spikes
- Small architecture sketch to reduce auth token races during rollout
- Quota backfill / fair-share edge case simulation plan
- Action items and owners for the week

Topline metrics snapshot (last 24h):
- p50 control plane RPC: 38ms (target 40ms)
- p95: 120ms (target 110ms) — small regression after canary 2026-08-29
- p99: 360ms (SLO 300ms) — outlier tail due to retry storm around 03:00 UTC
- Quota rejections: 0.6% of inbound requests (normal baseline 0.15%)
- Auth error rate (4xx token refresh): 0.9% spike correlated to kube rolling update of edge-auth-proxy

Quick diagnosis notes:
- Canary 2026-08-29 introduced a change to route cache invalidation that increases cold-start RPCs to the auth service. Those extra auth calls cause transient spikes and retries that propagate to p99.
- Retry storm started when node draining overlapped quota-trimming job; some clients retried aggressively (exponential backoff misconfigured in legacy client libs).
- Observability gaps: per-route token-refresh latency not surfaced in current dashboards; need a small tracing tag update to see where token waits occur.

Sketch: auth token refresh race (hand-wave ASCII)
- Client -> router -> auth-proxy -> token-service
- On route cache miss, router calls auth-proxy synchronously. If N inflight requests for same tenant & same prefix, token-service gets N requests.
- Proposed sketch: router-side dedupe cache (short coalescing window 50ms) + token-service idempotency key to collapse refresh flows.

Benefits: reduces auth-service qps spikes, reduces p99 tail during bursts, and avoids unnecessary quota accounting churn.
Tradeoffs: adds router memory for coalescing state and marginal additional latency for first request (aim <5ms).

Quota backfill / fair-share simulation plan (next 72h):
- Goal: test quota re-assignment when a new dedicated pool comes online and traffic gets rebalanced. Validate that shared quotas don't double-charge during overlap window.
- Steps:
  1) Create synthetic tenants A/B/C with steady traffic patterns (via loadgen).
  2) Introduce new dedicated pool for tenant B; trigger routing shift per canary policy.
  3) Run quota backfill job with controlled start/stop; assert no double-debits and no >1% spike in rejections.
  4) Run edge-case: client clients with stale token attempt to re-route -> expect auth-token-refresh path handled gracefully.
- Simulation owners: Marco (loadgen), Priya (quota assertions), Omar (routing policy config)
- Target run: start 2026-09-01 02:00 UTC, duration 4h for first pass

Open questions / risks:
- Should we prefer router-side coalescing or push dedupe entirely into token-service? (tradeoffs: single point of complexity vs cross-cluster state)
- How aggressive should coalescing window be? 20ms might miss spikes, 200ms might add latency for low-traffic users.
- Quota backfill: do we need a GC phase to reconcile counters post-backfill? (Priya thinks yes for corner cases)

Decisions made in meeting:
- Implement router-side 50ms coalescing prototype behind feature flag (Nina + Marco)
- Add tracing tag for token-refresh path and a short dashboard to capture per-route token-latency (Lydia)
- Run the quota backfill simulation next Wednesday (Omar to schedule orchestration)

Action items (owner — due):
- Nina: prototype router coalescing patch (feature-flagged) and rough perf run (due 2026-09-03) — JIRA: PLT-6721
- Marco: extend loadgen with tenant-level backpressure patterns + run smoke sim (due 2026-09-01)
- Priya: write assertion suite for quota double-debit detection and GC heuristics (due 2026-09-02)
- Omar: create routing policy canary config and schedule the simulation run (due 2026-08-31)
- Lydia: add tracing tags and a temporary Grafana panel for token-refresh latency (due 2026-09-02)
- Rahul (async): review token-service idempotency approach and note compatibility constraints (requested by 2026-09-04)

Notes to self / followups:
- Add a short paragraph to the control plane runbook about how to abort quota backfill if rejections > 2% for >10m.
- Add a small chaos test that drains router node during quota trim to reproduce the retry storm in CI.
- Check legacy client libs for retry/backoff config; reach out to SDK-maintainers to coordinate a rollback or client-side limiter if necessary.

References / pointers:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/891 (routing-cache invalidation change)
- Dashboards: /dashboards/controlplane/latency-overview (ask Lydia for temp panel)
- Slack thread with logs: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1693400000000

Status: draft — will convert to 'in_review' after initial prototyping results and loadgen run.

Small appendix: quick checklist for the router coalescing prototype
- [ ] feature flag gating (router.config.enable_coalesce)
- [ ] minimal in-memory coalescing table (weak-LRU) per router-worker
- [ ] 50ms timer + immediate collapse logic
- [ ] metrics: coalesce_hits, coalesce_misses, additional_coalesce_latency_ms
- [ ] unit tests for concurrent requests for same key

End of sketch. Push feedback into this doc as comments or drop notes in #platform-controlplane.
